t: What Distributed Mesh Computing Networks Is
title: What Distributed Mesh Computing Networks Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Distributed mesh computing networks turn collections of devices — phones, PCs, edge boxes — into one shared computer: workloads split across the mesh, migrate to where resources are free, and survive individual nodes dropping out. The network itself is the data center. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Distributed Mesh Computing Networks: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Distributed Mesh Computing Networks in one line: Distributed mesh computing networks turn collections of devices — phones, PCs, edge boxes — into one shared computer: workloads split across the mesh, migrate to where resources are free, and survive individual nodes dropping out.
Why it matters: They unlock the vast idle compute in the world's devices and keep working when infrastructure fails..
Where it is used: community clouds, disaster response, scientific computing, edge AI, decentralized services..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Distributed Mesh Computing Networks
title: Current Research State of Distributed Mesh Computing Networks
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Mesh protocols (libp2p, Yggdrasil), distributed schedulers, and projects like BOINC/Folding@home proved the model; WebRTC and QUIC enabled browser-node meshes. Research focuses on incentives, trustless verification, and latency-aware scheduling. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Distributed Mesh Computing Networks currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
